findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance and its underlying EBS storage/snapshots hold data in cleartext, exposing database contents to anyone with access to the storage layer or snapshots.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, dramatically expanding the attack surface of a database holding application data. The endpoint is also emitted as an output.

The master username is the predictable default 'admin' and the password is supplied via a Terraform variable that will be stored in cleartext in state and is reused verbatim in EC2 user data, making credential compromise likely.

No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error/general/slowquery) and no IAM database authentication are configured, so unauthorized access to the database cannot be detected or attributed, and password auth is the only control.

The EC2 user_data script writes the RDS master username and var.password in plaintext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc; user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF flaw on the host, leaking database master credentials.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled on an internet-facing web server; a server-side request forgery in the PHP application could retrieve the instance profile credentials for the highly privileged ec2role.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's EBS volume (which stores the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file) may be unencrypted at rest.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the EC2 instance profile. Combined with an internet-reachable web server running IMDSv1, a compromise of the instance yields account-wide control of all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases, including privilege escalation via ec2 actions.

Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, permitting unconstrained outbound connectivity that can be used for data exfiltration or command-and-control if the database host is compromised.
The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible database accepts unencrypted client connections and credentials/data can be transmitted in cleartext.
